```{r, include = FALSE}
# Network-dependent: nothing here is evaluated at build time.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  eval = FALSE
)
```

```{r setup, eval = TRUE}
library(geopt)
```

The bundled boundaries are simplified so they plot quickly. geopt can also
download data from the two official sources:

* **DGT** (Direção-Geral do Território): the full-resolution official boundaries (CAOP), and other datasets such as land cover, through its online service.
* **INE** (Instituto Nacional de Estatística): the census areas, from single city blocks upwards, with the census data attached.

Downloads go through `GeoClient`, an `R6` object that holds the settings, such as
where to cache:

```{r client}
client <- GeoClient$new()
client
```

Everything the client downloads is cached under
`tools::R_user_dir("geopt", "cache")`, so later calls are instant and work
offline. To use another folder, pass `GeoClient$new(cache_dir = ...)`.

If a download fails, because a server can't be reached or a file has moved,
the error says which and why:

```{r failed-download}
# With no internet connection
bgri <- get_censos("Braga")
#> Downloading Censos 2021 0303 (BGRI2021_0303.zip)...
#> Error: Could not reach mapas.ine.pt: Could not resolve hostname
#> [mapas.ine.pt]: Could not resolve host: mapas.ine.pt. Check your internet
#> connection, or try again later.
```

These errors have the class `geopt_download_error`, so a script can catch
failed downloads without hiding other errors. For example, to carry on with
the municipalities that did download:

```{r failed-download-catch}
bgri <- lapply(c("Braga", "Guimarães"), function(m) {
  tryCatch(get_censos(m), geopt_download_error = function(e) NULL)
})
```

## Full-resolution CAOP boundaries

```{r caop}
# Latest year, full detail, as sf
mun <- client$get_caop("continente", "municipio")

# A specific year and a simplification preset
freg_2022 <- client$get_caop("continente", "freguesia",
                             year = 2022, detail = "medium")
```

The regions are `"continente"`, `"raa"` (Açores) and
`"ram"` (Madeira). The levels run from `"freguesia"` to `"nuts3"`. When a
year's file has no NUTS layer, geopt builds it by merging municipalities.
`detail` simplifies the boundaries (`"full"`, `"high"`, `"medium"`, `"low"`
or `"very_low"`; this needs the rmapshaper package), and each combination is
cached.

To download the files without loading them, for example to read them with
other tools:

```{r download-only}
paths <- client$download_caop("continente", year = 2024)
```

## Filtered queries to DGT's online service

To get only part of a dataset, `get_ogc()` calls DGT's online service
(`https://ogcapi.dgterritorio.gov.pt`, which follows the OGC API standard) to
do the filtering, so the whole country isn't downloaded:

```{r ogc}
# One district's municipalities
lisboa <- client$get_ogc("municipios", properties = list(distrito = "Lisboa"))

# Everything inside a rectangle (longitude and latitude)
box <- client$get_ogc("freguesias", bbox = c(-9.3, 38.6, -9.0, 38.85))

# A filter expression, in the service's query language (CQL)
alg <- client$get_ogc("municipios", cql_filter = "distrito_ilha = 'Faro'")
```

The land cover maps (COS) and the land registry (`cadastro`) are large, so for
these a filter is **required**:

```{r cos}
cos <- client$get_ogc("cos2023v1", bbox = c(-8.45, 40.15, -8.35, 40.25))
```

To see what datasets the service offers right now:

```{r collections}
client$list_ogc_collections()
```

Raster datasets, such as aerial photographs, aren't supported yet. The error
message suggests how to read them with the terra package or GDAL instead.

## Census areas: subsecções, secções and the 1 km grid

INE publishes the areas the census is counted in, with the census data
attached to each file:

* **subsecções**, the smallest areas: city blocks in towns, villages or parts
  of villages in the countryside. They form the BGRI (Base Geográfica de
  Referenciação de Informação), available for the 1991, 2001, 2011 and 2021
  censuses.
* **secções**, statistical sections made of several subsecções.
* a **1 km grid**, for 2021 only.

`get_censos()` downloads the smallest file that covers the request: a
municipality is a 1–3 MB file, not a 250 MB download for the whole country.

```{r censos}
# City blocks of Braga, 2021 variables included
bgri <- get_censos("Braga")

library(ggplot2)
ggplot(bgri) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = N_INDIVIDUOS / as.numeric(sf::st_area(geometry)) * 1e6),
          color = NA) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "hab/km²", trans = "log10")
```

Choose the area with `municipio`, `freguesia` or `region` (a NUTS 2 or NUTS 3
name, `"continente"`, `"raa"`, `"ram"` or `"portugal"`). There's deliberately
no default, so the whole country can't be downloaded by accident.
The same call works for every census year and level:

```{r censos-variants}
# The 2011 census has 122 variables; keep only some
get_censos("Braga", year = 2011,
           variables = c("N_INDIVIDUOS_RESIDENT", "N_EDIFICIOS_CLASSICOS"))

# Secções: INE's 2021 files have about 180 variables.
# For earlier censuses, geopt merges the subsecções and adds up their counts.
get_censos("Braga", level = "seccao")
get_censos("Braga", level = "seccao", year = 2011)

# A NUTS3, and the 2021-only 1 km grid (region scope only)
get_censos(region = "Cávado")
get_censos(region = "continente", level = "grid")

# Data without geometry
get_censos("Braga", geometry = FALSE)
```

`pt_censos_vars` lists the variables for each year and level:

```{r censos-vars, eval = TRUE}
head(pt_censos_vars[pt_censos_vars$year == 2021 &
                      pt_censos_vars$level == "subseccao",
                    c("variable", "description")])
```

INE names its code columns differently in each census (`DTMN11` in 2011,
`DTMN21` in 2021, and so on). `get_censos()` adds the same codes under names
that stay the same every year (`bgri`, `dtmn`, `dtmnfr`, `seccao`,
`subseccao`, and `lugar` where the file has it), so results from different
censuses line up, and join with `pt_lookup()`. Each census uses the freguesias
of its own time, though, so the 2011 freguesia codes aren't today's: see
`vignette("vintages")`.

To use a client's cache and settings, pass it as
`get_censos("Braga", client = client)`.

## Exporting for dashboards

`export_boundaries()` writes GeoJSON or GeoPackage files, in WGS84 by default,
and can simplify the boundaries on the way out:

```{r export}
client$export_boundaries(mun, "municipios.geojson", detail = "low")
```

## Cache management

```{r cache}
client$list_cached()
client$clear_cache("processed")  # or "raw", "all"
```

## Relationship to the rest of geopt

`get_map()` and `plot_pt()` don't need the GeoClient for the current map:
they use the bundled boundaries. `get_map(admin_vintage = "2013")`, the one
earlier map they can draw, uses a `GeoClient` (and its cache) to download it
the first time it's needed.
